sections.title: Availability depends on engines
paragraphs: GET /v1/formats returns known formats, not a guarantee that every pair works. The server discovers routes up to three steps using installed engines. SVG and HEIC/HEIF are input-only. HEIC/HEIF requires macOS sips and is unavailable in the Linux Docker image.
sharp handles common raster formats; FFmpeg handles audio, video, and additional images; Poppler renders PDF pages; LibreOffice handles Office files. Query targets on the machine running conversion.

sections.title: Choose a route for your deployment
paragraphs: A route can combine multiple engines, such as converting an Office document to PDF and rendering a page as an image. Required tools must be installed on the same machine that runs the worker. A catalog entry alone does not guarantee that route.

HEIC and HEIF use macOS sips for decoding. The Linux Docker image cannot provide that macOS-only engine. Common raster, media, PDF, and Office workflows use the engines bundled in the image, subject to codec availability.

sections.title: Verify representative files
paragraphs: Test real input variants that your application expects before advertising a format. A container extension does not identify every possible media codec, and an Office format may contain features that render differently through LibreOffice.

Use a fixture conversion to validate each supported application workflow. For server-side PDF image output, specify one page; the CLI’s local batch workflow supports expanding multiple pages into separate outputs.
